scope: Actual v10 renderer mathematics and established antecedents; no claim that these named surfaces or formulas are new discoveries

primary_sources.title: Superquadrics and Angle-Preserving Transformations
primary_sources.author: Alan H. Barr
primary_sources.read_sections: Mathematical preliminaries; tangent/normal vectors; canonical superquadrics; superellipsoid position vectors; curvature-dependent sampling
primary_sources.used: Signed-power trigonometric superquadric parameterizations, tangent cross-product normals, and denser sampling near rapid geometric variation.
primary_sources.implementation_distinction: Normals here are finite differences recomputed after displacement, followed by barycentric interpolation. The inverse signed-power angular resampling and eight-family simulator are engineering implementations, not a reproduction of the full paper.

primary_sources.title: Mathematical Documentation of 3D-XplorMath: Torus Knots
primary_sources.read_sections: Torus Knots, PDF pages146-147; Trefoil Knot, page150
primary_sources.used: A torus-knot centerline c(u)=((R+r cos(3u))cos(2u),(R+r cos(3u))sin(2u),r sin(3u)); winding numbers2and3 give a trefoil.
primary_sources.implementation_distinction: The tube uses our periodic radial-projection frame, not the document's Frenet or parallel-transport frame; no external mesh or rendered image was used.

implemented_definitions.signed_powers: C_e(t)=sign(cos t)|cos t|^e, S_e(t)=sign(sin t)|sin t|^e
implemented_definitions.superellipsoid: (a C_e1(v) C_e2(u), b C_e1(v) S_e2(u), c S_e1(v))
implemented_definitions.supertoroid: ((R+r C_e2(v)) C_e1(u), (R+r C_e2(v)) S_e1(u), r S_e2(v))
implemented_definitions.lobed_vase: A z-dependent trigonometric/Gaussian radial profile revolved about z, modulated by cos(k u), plus toroidal rim and foot. It is an open wall, not a watertight vessel.
implemented_definitions.trefoil_tube: Sweep a circular section about the(2,3) torus-knot centerline. T=normalize(c'), N=normalize(q-(q dot T)T) with q=normalize(c_x,c_y,0), B=T cross N.
implemented_definitions.corrugated_torus: A torus with section radius r[1+a cos(k u+2v)], creating geometrically helical ribs.
implemented_definitions.saddle_shell: (a x,b y,c(x^2-y^2)+d sin(3x)cos(2y)), x,y in[-1,1]; open two-sided shell.
implemented_definitions.radial_rosette: A spherical radial function1+a cos(k u)cos(v)^2+b cos(m v), with independent height scaling.
implemented_definitions.multipart_spindle: Revolved Gaussian bulge r(t)=r0+b exp(-(t/w)^2), z=h t, plus three toroidal collars. Components intersect; they are not Boolean-unioned.
implemented_definitions.surface_displacement: S'=S+strength*f(u,v)*N, where f=.8 sum_j[w_j exp(-.5((du/sigma_u)^2+(dv/sigma_v)^2))]/sum_j|w_j|+.2 cos(k u+3v+phase)E(v). E=1 on periodic tubes and sin(pi v_normalized)^2 on open latitude coordinates. Thus |f|<=1.
implemented_definitions.normals: Normalize finite-difference du(S') cross dv(S'); recompute after geometric displacement. Interpolate normals barycentrically on visible triangles and normalize. Display normals face the camera for two-sided shading.
implemented_definitions.rasterizer: Dense parametric triangles, exact pixel-center coverage, barycentric depth and normals, frontmost z-buffer. Lambertian diffuse plus a bounded specular term; no Gaussian image blur, post-render resizing, or point-splat hole filling.

interpretation_limits: The Gaussian fields use parameter-domain distances, not intrinsic geodesic distances or a learned distribution of real object variation.
The surface names describe established primitives and our explicit compositions; novelty must be evaluated at the complete learning method and controlled results.
Two-view invariance and sensitivity to small synthetic geometric changes do not establish human-like cognition or natural-category recognition.
The renderer is orthographic and omits cast shadows, physical materials, topology validation, and true mesh Boolean union. Native128 rasterization still has ordinary pixel aliasing.
The held-out set contains unseen object seeds within the same eight surface families, not unseen mathematical families.
